module.title: Managed AI building blocks and platform choices
module.summary: Place foundation-model access, AI Functions, serving endpoints, the AI Gateway, Agent Bricks and custom agents by who writes the logic above the model, choose among them with five criteria rather than novelty, and record availability, cost and evaluation as dated assumptions.
objectives: Distinguish pay-per-token, provisioned-throughput and external-model access, AI Functions, Agent Bricks agents and custom agents by who writes the logic, who hosts it and who pays.

Choose a pattern for a knowledge assistant with a decision table on customization, data access, operations, evaluation and risk, including when a fixed retrieval workflow beats autonomous tool selection.
Record availability, release stage and cost as dated assumptions from named artifacts, and plan an evaluation that compares the alternatives on one labelled question set.

scenarios.title: Choose the managed pattern for Cinderline's maintenance-knowledge assistant
scenarios.context: Fictional Cinderline Components wants maintenance technicians on three press lines to ask questions of 2,400 equipment manuals and service bulletins stored as PDFs in a Unity Catalog volume, alongside a work-order history table. Technicians want cited answers on a tablet; the reliability lead also asks whether the assistant could check spare-part stock. Security requires that manual content never be sent to a third-party model provider, that every answer cite a manual revision, and that technicians see only their own plant's bulletins. The workspace's region, entitlements, release stages and prices are unconfirmed, and no model has been called.
scenarios.task: Write a one-page pattern selection for the platform owner: the recommended building block with two alternatives, a decision table, a responsibilities note saying who hosts, governs and pays, an availability and status table with unknown cells, a cost-assumption table that names drivers and says check current pricing, an evaluation plan built on a labelled question set, and the condition under which the team would move from retrieval to autonomous tool selection.
requirements: Compare at least three supported patterns on customization, data access, operations, evaluation and risk; do not rank by novelty.
Say who hosts, governs and pays for each component, including any external provider.
Mark release stage, cloud and region availability and workspace enablement as unknown until verified against a named, dated source; infer nothing from launch announcements.
Give cost drivers and synthetic volumes but no prices; every rate reads check current pricing.
Plan one labelled evaluation set run against every alternative, with blocking rules agreed before any result.
scenarios.model:
### Recommendation
First release: a **Knowledge Assistant** over the manuals volume (a files source) and the bulletin index, answering on a Databricks-hosted model. Named fallback: a **fixed retrieval workflow in code** (retrieve permitted passages, answer with a citation or refuse) if the assistant is not enabled in Cinderline's region. Deferred: a **Supervisor Agent** with a stock_lookup function, until stock or history questions reach one in five of labelled questions or live stock becomes a requirement. External models are excluded for manual content by the security rule.

### Decision table
| Pattern | Customization | Data access | Operations | Evaluation | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Knowledge Assistant | sources, instructions, examples | volume, index | platform-built; sync after new manuals | examples, labelled set, experiment | opaque internals; plant scoping to verify |
| Fixed workflow (code) | every step | the index we build | our team | labelled set, traces | our bugs and upkeep |
| Supervisor Agent | tools, descriptions | manuals plus stock | more tools to maintain | adds tool-call and denied-tool cases | wrong or denied tool on every question |

### Responsibilities
Databricks hosts the endpoints, the model and the assistant's orchestration, outside Cinderline's cloud account. Cinderline governs the volume, the index, the grants (CAN_QUERY for the tablet app's identity only) and the evaluation sign-off, and pays for usage. No third party receives manual text.

### Availability and status (unknown until verified)
| Item | Label found | Region | Workspace |
|---|---|---|---|
| Knowledge Assistant | Public Beta badge, Terraform provider v1.133.0 | unknown | unknown |
| Hosted model for this use | no label found | unknown | unknown |
| Per-technician document permissions in answers | not stated in artifacts read | not applicable | unknown |
| AI Gateway on the agent endpoint | SDK 0.141.0: inference tables only | not applicable | not applicable |

Because one assistant cannot yet be shown to respect plant permissions, sources are split per plant until that is verified. With one app identity holding CAN_QUERY on every plant's assistant, plant separation rests on the app: it selects each technician's plant assistant from the signed-in identity, never from a request field, and a two-plant test (a plant-2 technician asking for a plant-3 bulletin is refused) is an owned verification item. The alternative is to grant CAN_QUERY on each plant's assistant to that plant's users and call it with user authorization.

### Cost assumptions
Questions: 300 a day at about 3,400 tokens each; an index over 2,400 manuals; one agent endpoint; evaluation at 60 rows × 4 scorers × 10 runs. Every rate: check current pricing. After the pilot, usage-tracking system tables and endpoint tags replace these figures.

### Evaluation plan
Sixty labelled technician questions (46 manuals, 6 refusals, 5 stock, 3 history), with expected facts, sources and refusals labelled by a maintenance engineer. Both retrieval candidates run on the same rows with correctness, retrieval groundedness, safety and a citation guideline. Each row carries its caller, so refusal cases run as a technician of the asking plant. Blocking rules agreed now: every refusal case passes; no answer cites a superseded revision; correctness at least 0.85; an engineer reviews every failure. After release, the inference table is sampled into the set monthly.

### Switching condition
Pilot a Supervisor Agent when stock or history questions reach one in five, or when answers must use live stock. Drafting work orders waits for an authorization design.
scenarios.reasoning: The note filters on the hard security constraint first, compares three supported patterns on the same five criteria, prefers retrieval because the labelled mix shows one corpus answers most questions, keeps hosting, governing and paying apart, fills status cells only from named artifacts while leaving region, workspace and prices unknown, and fixes the evaluation and switching rules before any result exists.

rubric.weak: One pattern named, chosen because it is newest or most capable.
rubric.partial: Alternatives listed but compared on different criteria, or the security constraint ignored.
rubric.strong: Hard constraints filter first; three patterns compared on the same five criteria; a named fallback and a deferral with its trigger.

rubric.weak: Databricks is said to own everything because the compute is managed.
rubric.partial: Hosting and paying stated; governance of sources and grants missing.
rubric.strong: Hosts, governs and pays separated per component; no third party receives manual text; plant scoping owned by Cinderline.

rubric.weak: Availability or GA inferred from an announcement; prices quoted from memory.
rubric.partial: Unknowns mentioned in prose without a table, or some rates guessed.
rubric.strong: Status cells cite an artifact and date or read unknown; the cost table has drivers and volumes and check current pricing for every rate.

rubric.weak: Evaluation means trying a few questions after launch.
rubric.partial: A labelled set exists, but candidates run on different questions or rules are set after results.
rubric.strong: One labelled set for every candidate, blocking rules agreed in advance, engineer review, post-release sampling and a measurable switching condition.

disclosures.question: May manual text go to an external model provider if the endpoint lives in our workspace?
disclosures.response: No. The rule is about where the prompt is processed, not where the endpoint is configured; manual content stays on Databricks-hosted models.

disclosures.question: Is the Knowledge Assistant enabled in our workspace and region?
disclosures.response: Unknown. Nobody has checked yet; the platform owner will verify in the workspace and the current documentation before the design review.

disclosures.question: Do technicians need the assistant to create or draft work orders?
disclosures.response: Not in the first release. Drafting is a later wish; for now the assistant should link to the maintenance system.

claims.description: Foundation-model access on Databricks serving endpoints comes as pay-per-token endpoints, provisioned-throughput endpoints sized in model units with optional burst scaling, and external-model endpoints that forward to a named provider using a key referenced from a secret scope.
claims.context: SDK 0.141.0 and Terraform provider v1.133.0, read 2026-09-23.

claims.description: Pay-per-token is charged by tokens processed and suits getting started and variable volume; provisioned throughput provides dedicated capacity for production workloads that need predictable performance; availability of models and modes varies by region.
claims.context: Foundation Model APIs documentation as previously read; not fetched or search-confirmed in this build.

claims.description: Task-specific AI Functions such as ai_classify, ai_extract and ai_parse_document perform one task with a managed model, and ai_query sends each row's request to a serving endpoint the caller names.
claims.context: REST equivalents read in SDK 0.141.0; ai_query as previously read.

claims.description: Serving endpoints run on Databricks-managed serverless compute outside the customer's cloud account, hold served entities and traffic routes and grant CAN_QUERY to callers; the agent framework's deploy() puts a Unity Catalog agent model version on an agent endpoint with an inference table, keeping earlier versions served at zero traffic.

The serving-endpoint AI Gateway provides rate limits, guardrails, usage tracking in system tables, inference tables and fallback; SDK 0.141.0 says external-model, provisioned-throughput and pay-per-token endpoints are fully supported while agent endpoints currently support only inference tables, and the Terraform provider v1.133.0 page states a narrower, external-only scope.
claims.context: Dated statements from two artifacts in the same week; re-check current documentation.

claims.description: A Knowledge Assistant is configured with a description, optional instructions, knowledge sources (a vector search index, Unity Catalog volume files or a file table) and examples, and reports an agent endpoint, an MLflow experiment and a state; non-index sources must be synced. A Supervisor Agent routes requests among configured tools such as Knowledge Assistants, Genie spaces, Unity Catalog functions, MCP connections and apps.
claims.context: SDK 0.141.0, read 2026-09-23; answer quality and identities per tool not stated.

claims.description: A custom agent wraps its own logic in MLflow's ResponsesAgent interface, which can wrap any agent framework, and is deployed to an agent endpoint with the Mosaic AI Agent Framework SDK.

The Terraform provider v1.133.0 labels the Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent resources Public Beta and states that its provisioned-throughput endpoint resource is in private preview for enrolled customers; these are dated labels on named artifacts, not availability for any workspace, region or cloud.

mlflow.genai.evaluate runs built-in scorers such as Correctness, RetrievalGroundedness, Safety and Guidelines, and custom scorers, over labelled rows, traces or inputs passed to a predict function; Knowledge Assistants carry examples with guidelines and an MLflow experiment.

AI Gateway usage tracking records operational usage on endpoints and associated costs in system tables and endpoint tags propagate to billing logs; no artifact read states a rate, so rates come from current pricing.
claims.context: SDK 0.141.0 and Terraform provider v1.133.0, read 2026-09-23.

concepts.definition: One of the platform's ways to put a model to work, distinguished by who writes the logic between request and model.
How an application reaches a model: per-token hosted endpoints, reserved provisioned capacity, or an endpoint forwarding to an outside provider.
SQL-callable functions that apply a model to each row, either for a fixed task or against a serving endpoint the caller names.
A Model Serving endpoint hosting an agent version, answering REST queries from identities that hold CAN_QUERY.
Configuration on serving endpoints for rate limits, guardrails, usage tracking, inference tables and fallback, whose support varies by endpoint type.
Databricks agents configured from sources, tools, instructions and examples rather than written as code.
Agent logic written as code, logged with MLflow, registered in Unity Catalog and deployed to an agent endpoint by the team that owns it.
A pipeline that always retrieves permitted passages and answers from them with citations, or refuses, taking the same steps for every question.
A design in which a model chooses per request which tools to call, adding a routing decision that can be wrong.
The separation between who runs a component, who decides its data and access, and who is charged for it.
A dated label on a named artifact describing a feature's support level, distinct from availability in a given cloud, region or workspace.
An estimate that multiplies countable volumes by named drivers and leaves every rate to current pricing.
One set of labelled questions with expected facts, sources and refusals, run against every candidate under rules agreed in advance.
